item.text:
**1B.6 Research Note: Ali Khamenei in 2024**

**Bottom line:** I found **weak positive evidence** that the official nuclear line still rejected proliferation, but **stronger evidence that hardliners in Khamenei’s orbit were publicly pushing toward doctrinal change** under threat. I did **not** find direct 2024 evidence that Khamenei had to stop a proxy or client from proliferating nuclear capabilities. On balance, this lens is **not well supported as affirmative**.

**Accepted claims**

| Title | Publisher | Date | Recoverable URL | Claim-level summary | Question IDs |
|---|---|---:|---|---|---|
| `Iran says nuclear weapons have no place in its nuclear doctrine` | Reuters | 2024-04-22 | [link](https://www.theprint.in/world/iran-says-nuclear-weapons-have-no-place-in-its-nuclear-doctrine/2051387/) | Iran’s foreign ministry publicly said nuclear weapons were not part of Iran’s doctrine, and Reuters noted Khamenei’s long-standing fatwa banning nuclear weapons. This is the clearest 2024 evidence that the regime publicly resisted proliferation at the doctrinal level. | `1B.6`, `1B.2`, `1B.4` |
| `Iranian commander warns Tehran could review 'nuclear doctrine' amid Israeli threats` | Reuters | 2024-04-18 | [link](https://www.theprint.in/world/iranian-commander-warns-tehran-could-review-its-nuclear-doctrine/2046641/) | Ahmad Haghtalab, the commander in charge of nuclear security, said Israeli threats could push Tehran to review and deviate from its nuclear doctrine. This shows domestic hardliners publicly pressing in the opposite direction, which weakens any claim that Khamenei firmly resisted proliferation pressure. | `1B.6`, `1B.2`, `1B.3` |
| `Iran to change nuclear doctrine if existence threatened, adviser to supreme leader says` | Reuters | 2024-05-09 | [link](https://www.dawn.com/news/1832474) | Kamal Kharrazi, an adviser to Khamenei, said Iran would alter its nuclear doctrine if its existence were threatened. That is strong evidence that a domestic faction around Khamenei was willing to trade against restraint when short-term political and security interests shifted. | `1B.6`, `1B.2` |
| `US still believes Iran has not decided to build a nuclear weapon, US officials say` | Reuters | 2024-10-11 | [link](https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/us-still-believes-iran-has-not-decided-to-build-a-nuclear-weapon-us-officials-say-3659043) | U.S. officials told Reuters that Iran still had not decided to build a nuclear weapon despite setbacks to its allies and regional position. This is indirect, but it supports the view that Khamenei had not allowed the current crisis environment to convert into an actual proliferation decision. | `1B.6` |

**Assessment**

- The **positive** evidence is mostly declaratory: official doctrine still rejected nuclear weapons.
- The **negative** evidence is more specific: a nuclear-security commander and a Khamenei adviser publicly floated doctrine change if threatened.
- I found **no reliable 2024 evidence** of Khamenei personally blocking a proxy, client, or allied faction from pursuing nuclear proliferation, nor evidence that such a group had an active nuclear program requiring suppression.
- So the safest reading is **weak/partial resistance in doctrine, but no demonstrated hard resistance to proliferation pressure in practice**.

**Search gap**

- I did **not** find 2024 evidence showing an ally, proxy, or client trying to proliferate nuclear capability and Khamenei stopping it.
- The available material is centered on **domestic elite rhetoric** and official doctrine, not on actual third-party proliferation attempts.
